reason: shadcn's chart.tsx is a themed wrapper (ChartContainer, ChartStyle, ChartTooltipContent, ChartLegendContent) around recharts, a React-only library whose charts are drawn by React components that register in a redux store from effects. (1) shadcn-port R14 asks for a pinned JS equivalent behind a Stimulus controller; it is NOT followed because the maintainer constraint of the adoption epic is no third-party JavaScript (the same constraint as sonner) and because recharts renders an EMPTY wrapper under react-dom renderToStaticMarkup (measured by dev/spikes/chart: its items register in useEffect, which never runs on the server), so a vendored engine could not produce server-rendered charts at all. Instead the chart is a Phlex SVG that emits the DOM recharts 3.8 produces after the browser settles (class names, group order, attributes), the math recharts uses (getNiceTickValues, band/point scales, stacks, curveMonotoneX and the other d3-shape curves, sectors) is ported to Ruby, and the behavior (tooltip, cursor, keyboard, legend) is the small chadcn--chart controller reading data-* attributes. The spike reproduces the stacked bar and monotone line DOM with a largest numeric deviation of 0.0 px (decision record: dev/decisions/chart.md). (2) Sizing: recharts' ResponsiveContainer measures its parent and re-lays out the chart on every resize; the server cannot measure, so ChartContainer lays the chart out at initial_dimension (default 320x200, the shadcn default) and draws it at that pixel size (.recharts-wrapper width/height in px, the DOM recharts writes at that container size). With relayout_url: (item #107, dev/decisions/chart.md 'Resize and re-measure') chadcn--chart observes the box, waits until it settles (150 ms), requests the chart at the rounded size from that same-origin URL and swaps the answer in, so the chart follows its container with recharts' DOM at the new size (browser test against recharts resized from 320 to 480 and 640 px; G2 compares the resize__* scenarios at 320, 480 and 640); between the resize and the answer the previous layout is scaled into the box (viewBox, CSS only), boxes over 4096 px stay scaled, and an error answer keeps the scaled chart and stops re-laying out that element. Without relayout_url: (the default), before the first answer and without JavaScript the chart keeps initial_dimension whatever its container does; the host chooses the size with initial_dimension:. G2 compares the server render at the scenario's initial dimension. (3) No animation: recharts animates the first paint (isAnimationActive 'auto', 400 to 1500 ms); the Phlex chart renders the final state and never animates (isAnimationActive is accepted and ignored), and the oracle renders with isAnimationActive false so both sides compare the settled state. (4) JSON-only scenarios: the parity scenarios are JSON trees rendered by both harnesses, which cannot carry React elements or functions, so a chart scenario is data: the shadcn layer is named by its export (ChartContainer, ChartTooltip, ChartLegend, ChartStyle; the contents are the value of content) and the recharts parts are harness-scoped _-prefixed nodes (_BarChart, _Bar, _XAxis, _Label ...) resolved by a probes module on the React side and by ShadcnParity::TreeRenderer#harness_scope on the Phlex side; functions (tickFormatter, labelFormatter, formatter) are expressed as the named formatters of the spec ({formatter: slice, args: [start, end]} = JS String#slice and Ruby slicing with the same clamping as JS String#slice (spec: Named formatters), locale, percent; Ruby kwarg form {slice: [start, end]}), the Ruby classes also accept any callable. (5) Text measurement: recharts measures labels, the legend box and the tooltip with the DOM (getStringSize, getBoundingClientRect); the server lays out with a line box, an average glyph width and a legend height (kwargs on ChartContainer: text_height 16, text_char_width 0.6em, legend_height nil = the Legend's 28) and chadcn--chart measures the tooltip box (its position is computed in the browser). Re-measure needs relayout_url: (item #108, dev/decisions/chart.md 'Resize and re-measure'): after document.fonts.ready and on every settled size chadcn--chart measures the tick text the way recharts does (a white-space: pre span under body at the tick's font size and letter spacing) and the legend box, and when they differ from the metrics the server laid out with it requests the chart at those metrics (one request per size for the metrics alone, so a host that ignores them cannot loop); the server then decides which tick labels exist, their positions and the plot area from the measured metrics (browser test chart_remeasure.test.mjs: in a monospace font with 14px lines and 14px letter spacing the swapped chart equals recharts, its dropped month labels included). What stays: without relayout_url:, before the answer and without JavaScript the assumed metrics decide; a label's width is estimated as its length times the measured average glyph width where recharts measures each string (a label within that margin of the collision threshold can be kept or dropped differently in a proportional font). G2 compares the server render at the parity page's measured line height (text_height 18). (6) Tooltip: ChartTooltipContent is rendered once per category index as an inert template (server, per-index) and the controller shows the one for the active index; the position of the tooltip wrapper (style, -top/-right class modifiers) is the controller's output and excluded from G2. (7) Legend height: Chart::Legend legend_height: is the server's assumption for the measured legend box (default 28 = pt-3 + one 16px line); re-measure needs relayout_url: (Chart::Container legend_height:, read from the request by relayout_options, wins over it; a numeric Legend height: wins over both). (8) Behavior not ported: ref, onClick/onMouseMove style callbacks as props (events instead), custom React-element content (content={<Custom/>}), Brush, ReferenceLine/ReferenceArea/ErrorBar, syncId, Customized, and every prop that takes a React element or function other than the named formatters. Cartesian tooltip (item #48): the axis event type has one template per category; `shared: false` on a BarChart resolves recharts' item event type (state/selectors/selectTooltipEventType.js:4-13, chart/BarChart.js:5), drawn since item #109 as one template per bar series and category, with every bar (and its background) tagged as a tooltip item so chadcn--chart shows the series under the pointer alone, placed at the bar's center, as recharts does (context/tooltipContext.js); on LineChart and AreaChart (axis only) shared: false stays an axis tooltip, as in recharts. The wrapper's position (`transform`) is left to the controller, since it depends on the measured size of the content. Parity runs at text_height 18 (the shared parity page is not font-pinned and recharts measures tick text 18px high there; ShadcnParity::ChartScope::PAGE_TEXT_HEIGHT); the gem default 16 is unit-tested (text_height_test.rb), not G2-gated, until the runner page is pinned for chart scenarios. Controller (item #50): the post-font-load re-measure pass of (5) was built by item #108 as a re-layout request (no axes value, no tickTemplate children: the server decides which tick labels exist from the measured metrics; spec, Behavior, Resize and re-measure); the tooltip interaction (pointer, touch, click trigger, keyboard, Escape, default_index precedence, placement, cursor and active dots, Turbo cache) is. A pie's item tooltip makes the controller inert (its sectors are not tagged as tooltip items): it never touches the wrapper, so a pie's server-drawn tooltip stays as drawn. A chart outside a Chart::Container is not wired (no controller element to carry the values). Polar charts (item #49): the polar tooltip has no cursor, because recharts draws it from the polar coordinate of the pointer, which a server render does not have; `data-coordinate` of a radar or radial bar template is recharts' own default-index anchor (the middle of the chart across, the tick's angle or radius along), which recharts marks as unsound; `shared: false` on a radial bar chart resolves recharts' item event type (chart/RadialBarChart.js:11) and is drawn like a BarChart's since item #109 (the arcs are tagged and their wrapper hears the pointer, not the keys: a polar chart has no keyboard layer yet; an arc has no tooltipPosition, so the tooltip is placed at the default_index anchor or not at all, as in recharts), and stays axis on a radar (chart/RadarChart.js:11); apart from those arcs chadcn--chart maps the pointer and the keys for the cartesian charts only: a polar chart publishes its tooltip values alone (Polar::Wiring, item #85: no ticks, no data-action), a pie as item (the controller is inert and the server-drawn tooltip is untouched), a radar and a radial bar as axis (the controller keeps, places and restores the default_index tooltip; nothing moves it); a radar range (`[low, high]` values), `active_shape:` and `stack_offset:` are not ported; the polar axes take no `hide:` (recharts does not read it) and the angle axis no `tick_count:` (it has no nice ticks); only `fill`, `stroke`, `name` and `opacity` of a data row reach its sector, as for a bar.
api: Chart::Container relayout_url: re-lays the chart out on the server at the settled size of its box (chadcn--chart requests the chart from that same-origin URL and swaps it in; between the resize and the answer the previous layout is scaled into the box, where ResponsiveContainer re-lays out in the next frames); without relayout_url:, before the first answer and without JavaScript the chart is laid out once at initial_dimension: and drawn at that pixel size
isAnimationActive and every animation* prop of the series are accepted and ignored: the settled state is rendered (the tooltip wrapper keeps recharts' own 400 ms transform transition)
tick_formatter:, label_formatter:, formatter: accept a callable or a named formatter (slice, locale, percent) instead of a JavaScript function; React-element content is not supported
Chart::Tooltip content is rendered per category index as an inert template and swapped by chadcn--chart; tooltip position and wrapper class modifiers are computed in the browser

Chart::Legend legend_height: is the server's assumption for the measured legend box (default 28 = pt-3 + one 16px line); re-measure needs relayout_url: (chadcn--chart measures the box and the request's legend_height reaches Chart::Container legend_height:, which wins over it)

Chart naming (naming-conventions R2, open for the maintainer): chart names keep the Chart suffix (Chart::BarChart, not Chart::Bar) because Chart::Bar, Line, Area, Pie, Radar and RadialBar are the series classes of the same React names; de-stuttering would make two React exports share one Ruby constant

Chart::Container text_height:, text_char_width: and legend_height: are the server's metrics for DOM text measurement (assumptions 16, 0.6em and the Legend's 28); re-measure needs relayout_url: (chadcn--chart measures them after document.fonts.ready and requests the chart at the measured metrics); a label's width is its length times the average glyph width, where recharts measures each string
Chart::Config is a Hash of key => { label:, icon:, color: or theme: { light:, dark: } } (ChartConfig); icon is a component instance instead of a React component type
Brush, ReferenceLine, ReferenceArea, ErrorBar, Customized, syncId, ref and mouse/touch callback props are not ported
Chart::Tooltip::Content and Chart::Legend::Content accept **attrs on their root div (shadcn-port R6); React's ChartTooltipContent/ChartLegendContent do not spread props

Chart::Cell renders nothing itself (recharts Cell is () => null) but, as in recharts, its props are spread into the parent's shape at its index: it accepts **attrs (class: included) like every part and the parent lands them on that sector or rectangle (no R6 exception)
Chart::Style takes no attrs: it renders a bare <style> like ChartStyle
Chart::Tooltip and Chart::Legend class: and attrs are a chadcn addition on .recharts-tooltip-wrapper / .recharts-legend-wrapper (recharts has no className there)

Chart::Tooltip item_sorter:, separator: and content_style: are accepted and ignored with Chart::Tooltip::Content: recharts applies itemSorter, separator and contentStyle only inside DefaultTooltipContent (not ported), a custom content gets the payload unsorted; likewise Chart::Legend icon_size:, icon_type: and inactive_color: are ignored by Legend::Content
Chart::Tooltip formatter: / label_formatter: set on the Tooltip override the ones of its content: (recharts cloneElements the content with the Tooltip props)

Chart::Style raises ArgumentError for an id or config key outside [A-Za-z0-9_-] and for a color containing < > { } ; \ or /*, where React's ChartStyle interpolates any key and color into the style text untouched (ruby-gem-conventions R12)

Parity gate G2b (parity_run.mjs --dx helpers) is not run for chart until the tree renderer supports the harness-scoped _ nodes in its helpers mode (item #47); the helper path is covered by the unit test meanwhile

Chart::Tooltip active:, trigger:, offset:, allow_escape_view_box:, reverse_direction:, position:, wrapper_style: and the animation kwargs reach the browser as Stimulus values on div[data-slot=chart]; Tooltip portal:, use_translate3d:, item_style:, label_style: and the default contents DefaultTooltipContent / DefaultLegendContent are not ported

allow_tokens lists plain words of the ArgumentError messages in chart/scale/band.rb and chart/scale/linear.rb ("domain: and range: take two values each", "range: takes two values") that the G1 token scan reads as Tailwind classes because the static gate scans every file under lib/chadcn/chart; they are not class tokens

Chart::PieChart, Chart::RadarChart and Chart::RadialBarChart keep the Chart suffix (naming exception above) and draw recharts' polar DOM from Ruby; Chart::Pie, Chart::Radar, Chart::RadialBar, Chart::PolarGrid, Chart::PolarAngleAxis and Chart::PolarRadiusAxis are declarations (they render nothing where they are written and register with their chart)

Chart::Pie label: draws the values beside the sectors itself (label: true, or a Hash with offset_radius: and text attributes); a Hash with position: is a Chart::LabelList; label_line: is true, false or a Hash of attributes

Chart::Tooltip in a polar chart: one inert template per sector (pie), per angle / ring category (radar, radial bar), or per ring category and radial bar series (a radial bar chart with Tooltip shared: false, the item tooltip, as on a BarChart); there is no cursor; on a radar shared: false stays an axis tooltip
Chart::LabelList::POSITIONS gains outside, center_top, center_bottom, inside_start, inside_end and end; recharts' camelCase spellings (insideStart) are accepted for every position
